title: Chapter 279: I've Been Waiting for You
html:
Uncle Wong and Xiao Gu were sent to the hospital, while Chen Ge remained behind to help the task force wrap up its work at Fang Hwa Apartments. His diligence greatly improved the officers’ opinion of him.

Standing in the apartment opposite Room 3239, Chen Ge waited until the officers were looking elsewhere before taking out his phone. The black phone had vibrated when Zhang Ya transformed the man with the ruined face into a doll, but the situation had been too dangerous for him to check it.

A new message waited on the screen. With the man with the ruined face dealt with, the Third Sick Hall’s completion rate had risen to eighty percent!

If the completion rate reaches ninety percent, there will be a reward, so I need another ten percent.

Chen Ge studied the phone. Once the completion rate surpassed ninety percent, he would receive the Trial Mission reward. If he completely destroyed the Ghost Stories Society, he would earn the reward for the Third Sick Hall’s hidden mission as well.

In other words, the black phone is deliberately pitting me against the Ghost Stories Society. Why does it hate them so much?

His repeated encounters with the Society had deepened Chen Ge’s understanding of its members. Each served as a vessel for a monster from behind the door. To feed those monsters—or, more precisely, to keep the creatures attached to them from devouring them—they had to create ghost stories continually.

From one perspective, they were no longer human at all, but puppets controlled by monsters. That was the greatest difference between Chen Ge and most Society members.

I have a feeling the Society is more complicated than it appears. Their flyer depicts a bloodred door. Those lunatics must know far more about the world behind the door than I do. The mysterious chairperson might even be a ghost who came through one.

A sense of danger gripped Chen Ge. The employees currently working at his Haunted House no longer seemed sufficient.

“Xiao Chen!” The door swung open, and Captain Yan entered. Chen Ge immediately pocketed the black phone and slumped against the sofa, feigning weakness.

“Captain Yan, you’re looking for me?”

“See for yourself.” Captain Yan removed Xiao Gu’s phone from an evidence bag. About twenty-five minutes earlier, a peculiar message had arrived through WeChat: “Chen Ge, I’ll remember your name.”

“It was sent from the security guard Wang Dajun’s phone. We searched the entire twenty-third floor but couldn’t find the device. We therefore suspect another culprit escaped with it.” Captain Yan placed Xiao Gu’s phone on the coffee table. “That raises another question: why does the message mention you by name?”

Wang Dajun was Uncle Wong’s full name. It was because of him that Xiao Gu had entered the third building.

“Whoever took Uncle Wong’s phone must be the mastermind—the person who planned everything tonight.” Chen Ge understood the message. The culprit had planned meticulously but underestimated Zhang Ya’s power and Chen Ge’s caution. If Zhang Ya had not come to his aid, or if either apartment had drawn him inside, he would have died.

The thought sent a shudder through him.

“The culprit sent this message, which tells us two things. First, he’s fearless. Second, you’ve enraged him deeply.” Captain Yan returned the phone to its evidence bag. “Neither is good news. He may seek even more extreme revenge.”

The Ghost Stories Society had lost four members at once. Even the man with the ruined face, who controlled two Red Specters, had been turned into a doll. If Chen Ge were one of the surviving members, he would have been furious too.

“Remember my name? Is that a threat?” Chen Ge watched Captain Yan turn to leave. A realization flashed through his mind, and he sprang from the sofa. “Wait!”

“What is it?” Chen Ge’s sudden movement startled Captain Yan.

“The phone—the time the message was sent!” Chen Ge took the evidence bag from him and checked the device. The message had been sent twenty-five minutes ago.

Twenty-five minutes earlier, the man with the ruined face had just died, and Lee Zheng’s team had not yet arrived!

“Another Society member was hiding in this building, and that person was probably the true mastermind!” Chen Ge’s eyes narrowed. The culprit had witnessed everything but remained hidden because of Zhang Ya.

“The culprit is still in the building?” Captain Yan nodded. “We control every exit, and the roads leading to and from Fang Hwa Apartments are sealed. We haven’t found anyone suspicious yet. Don’t worry—if the culprit is still here, they won’t escape.”

The final three Society members would be the most difficult to handle. Chen Ge could not simply place all his hopes in Captain Yan and his officers. He clenched his hands until his knuckles cracked. Something was missing.

The man is very clever. The message was sent twenty-five minutes ago, and he might have left already, but how did he escape the detection of the police?

As Chen Ge stared at the message in Xiao Gu’s WeChat, another detail returned to him. Xiao Jia had gone berserk after reading it, whereas the investigator who saw it first had merely collapsed. Their reactions had been entirely different.

“Captain Yan, what happened to the investigator who entered the building first? Who has been taking care of him?”

“When I last saw him, he was lying inside the police car, still unconscious. Twenty minutes ago, the ambulance arrived, so he’s probably at the hospital now.”

“Twenty minutes ago, the ambulance arrived?”

…

The nurses’ station stood silent. At two in the morning, the People’s Hospital was deathly quiet. Most patients were asleep when a pair of pure-white eyes slowly opened.

“Chen Ge…” The name escaped his lips involuntarily. Then he sat upright like a sleepwalker. “This new scapegoat’s body isn’t bad, but splitting my consciousness is unbearably painful.”

He clenched his fists, his expression turning sinister. A trace of envy colored his voice. “No matter how good a scapegoat is, it can never compare to a Red Specter.”

The man climbed out of bed and lurched toward the door like a poorly strung puppet. As he adjusted to the body, his pace gradually quickened.

With no one watching, he slipped into the hospital’s emergency stairwell, avoided every camera in the lobby, and emerged into the dark alley behind the building.

“Three hours left, I should have enough time to return to the main persona.”

He staggered through the alley, its ground strewn with gravel and refuse. Scratches covered his arms and feet, but he paid them no mind. As the exit drew closer, his body slowly relaxed.

“It doesn’t matter that the plan failed. As long as I survive and deliver the message, the outcome remains undecided.”

The streetlamps beyond the alley cast a sickly yellow glow. Just as the man neared the exit, a figure carrying a hammer stepped from the shadows and blocked his path.

“I’ve been waiting for you.”
